I'll start by briefly defining what made Dark Souls as great as it was....

In 2009, Demon's Souls, Dark Souls' predecessor, was released and adored in the West, but not so much in the East. This reaction led to the creation, but most importantly the release of Dark Souls in 2011. This game would go on to receive the "Greatest game of all time" award, cementing itself as a pillar of "modern" gaming. Seeing the immense success of the game, a sequel was ordered. However, the director had decided to work on another game. The task to direct Dark Souls 2 was given to one, passed to another and finally was finished and released in 2014. Yet again, the public loved it and complimented the greatness of the game. Nearly perfect scores by some critics, though the fanbase itself would end up being very divided on the game. Then, the year 2015 came along, with a re-release of Dark Souls 2. Only one year later, Dark Souls 3 came out. 

I had played Dark Souls 1 for nearly 1300 hours, and Dark Souls 2 for ~800 at the time of my first experience with Dark Souls 3. I LOVED both prequels to an unimaginable extent. It was nearly an obsession. I thought that, if the 2 others were this grand, and that, in my opinion, Dark Souls 2 was a major improvement on Dark Souls 1, surely Dark Souls 3 would be the greatest game of all time! I was severely mistaken, though...

Dark Souls (the series) relied on slow-pace combat and encouraged the player to pay attention to small details and worry about positioning. The combat was simple: Light and heavy attacks, directional dodges based on camera lock, two hands for one weapon/tool each. Simple as that. It worked so well and Dark Souls 2 kept it, adding more options for using both hands for weapons, as well. The combat was a test of patience and adaptability (not the attribute in DS2) more so than skill. The games were grounded, slow and clunky, but felt good to play. Then, Dark Souls 3 came out. Following the success of Bloodborne, released in 2014, worked on at the same time as Dark Souls 2, Dark Souls 3 would reimagine the combat, a signature element of the series so far. The game became less focused on adventure, with a linear map. Less focused on characters, by using simple archetypes or returning faces. Less focused on being creative and different, reusing animations, designs and move sets from previous games. It instead focused on the bosses. While the combat in Dark souls was always central, it wasn't the biggest or main selling point. Players, however, loved the bosses the most, as they stood as tests for the player to see how far they've come. However, the games also had expansive worlds and so many options handed to the player, whether it be the path you take or the quests you do. Dark Souls 3 forces you down a straight line, with very few optional areas. The few that are there are hidden, as well, making it seem like the game is one long road with a few bosses. Despite the game shifting focus on the bosses, changing the core feeling of the combat to something quicker and more floaty, in my opinion, it failed dramatically at making quality bosses. The 2 others had walked away from the pure gimmick fights of Demon's Souls, focusing on action combat instead, but still kept it slow and gimmicky at times. Dark Souls 3 fails its gimmick fights horribly, though. The game would excel at making fast-paced battles work with its movement, but the low amount of total bosses means a high percentage of them are failed gimmick fights, which are sad callbacks to when they could work in the others. Even then, the fights it took from were already laughably easy or bad in the other games, so it dug its grave deeper by not adapting to its own changes. It tried to stray from the old school Dark Souls, but its roots were firmly planted in the path it dearly wished not to follow. The action packed fights also tend to fail, in my opinion, by their design. The other games had a lot of room for adaptation. Dark Souls 3 wants you to play a certain way, and not doing so will make it much worse to play through the game.

The game also suffers from bugs. So many bugs. The most glaring and apparent issue is the shader problem. It's commonly joked about that the game looks grey. Well, yeah, it does. Because the game has a massive problem with its shaders. There's some grey filter over the whole game. Colors stand out more when they're allowed through, but overall, every area has one dominant color, which works artistically and story-wise, but gets exceedingly boring when you walk out of a grey castle to enter a grey village, to reach a grey church through a brown and grey swamp. This isn't hyperbolic, I described the path from the High Wall to the Cathedral, while being kind enough to leave the Cemetery and Shrine out of it. Outside of that, it suffers a lot from its quicker gameplay being affected by framerate. This can cause attacks to flail and their hitboxes to break. The camera was always awkward, but this game pushes it up to 11. Entities that chase you and are outside of your PoV will teleport behind you at times, especially noticeable on dogs. The Nameless King has an attack that can be completely ignored if you pan your camera away and leave him out of frame. This does NOT happen in the other games. It also has horrible collision problems. The ground sometimes stops working, and you either float or fall through, running attacks with greatswords on illusory walls can send you through the floor, I've clipped through walls and floor with ladders, and the Lothric Castle area has walls without collisions that have crossbow-wielding soldiers behind it, who can spot and shoot you through said walls. While minor, these issues pile up and can drastically affect the player's experience. All the issues I described happened to me, and those are all from my first playthrough. Some happened on other characters too. The game also has a problem with textures and when to load them. Going down the huge ladder in the Profaned Capital, if you look down, the floor's textures take a while to load sometimes, letting you see a mushy and ugly textures mess. The same happens with the wall near the Mercenary's Armor set in the Crucifixion Woods. There are many areas that let you see from up close the out-of-bounds sections, which are very poorly textured and low quality. This is excusable, but they could have tried to keep it out of clear and plain sight. The other games, while older, manage to mostly avoid the issue, or cover it up with some scenery. 

I wanted to love this game. I tried. For around 250 hours I tried and couldn't. This will forever be my least favorite game of the series. Dark Souls 2 is often called the black sheep, but Dark Souls 3 is far more deserving of the title, for being so blindingly different to its predecessors. It lost the core formulas and wasted most chances it got. The DLCs are fine, but do not excuse or redeem the mess that the base game is, because the central issues remain present. I will forever be disappointed that this is what we were given as a close to my favorite game series of all time. As unpopular as my opinion is, I feel shame saying I love the series, only because this game is part of it. 

If you like it, that's fine. I won't judge or hate you for it. However, some of its issues cannot be ignored and as much as I wish I could look past them, it's impossible for me to recommend the game, even to fans of the genre that came from the other FromSoftware titles. This game isn't a complete disgrace, but it has tarnished my opinion of the series as a whole severely enough to not be forgiven.

negative.original: I was expecting and hoping that this would recapture the joy i experienced in the first half of the original Dark Souls. It did not. The combat is faster and more jumpy. Initially it seems like it's less tactical, since enemies can just jump around obstacles. But you can learn to deal with that, I guess. And then you realize that "distance from opponents" is the key thing, so you have a new tactic to use. Although i found the combat kind of dull, I was hoping that maybe I could gear my character in a way that was fun. Unfortunately, I thought all the armor looks like clunky junk. Armor values never seemed to matter, so I was looking to wear that looks good. Early on, i was using the Loin Cloth and Evangelist Hat. But eventually i saw a couple of mobs whose gear i thought looked cool! But i was horribly disappointed that i couldn't get the armor that looks as good on me. Both the Pontiff Knight (with those great gossamer wing / cape things) and the Jailer Handmaid (with those flowing robes) looked great on the enemies, but they don't let me wear those outfits and they look like hot garbage on the player model. So, at that point i just decided this isn't any fun and i stopped. What's the point of fighting, if you can't look good while doing it? I only got a little bit into the Painted World DLC, because i was pretty bored and gave up on the game by the time i got around to it. Maybe it's the best thing ever but i'll never know.

negative.original:
One of the best soulslikes i've ever played. Ruthless, but 95% of the time fair. The atmosphere, level design, bosses, everything is great. Coming from Elden Ring i can see how the latter is an improvement on all the good from the former.

Why the bad rating then? One big reason and it's not even for the game itself but for the absolutely horrendous PC port: no keyboard translations, no borderless window mode, no static camera follow-up, no normal mouse speed settings (only extremely fast even on 0), hardcoded "move forward + light attack" kick which leads to misclicks. Jesus, it doesn't even have a steam's cloud save (!!!). 10 years have passed and not a single issue was addressed. And spare me with your "bUt yOu sHoUlD pLaY iT oN cOnTrOlLeR", literally any other soulslike i've played works great with keyboard and mouse and doesn't have these problems. Thank god offline mode and mods exist so i managed to fix most of that sh*t myself.

If the above ever gonna be fixed (although i highly doubt it) i'll gladly change my rating. Fromsoft guys are actual game design geniuses, created the whole gamebreaking genre, but couldn't figure out simple qol stuff until elden ring...

negative.original: Second FromSoft game and hopefully i learned my lesson enough to not buy a third. It feels like the devs go out of their way to make it a miserable experience. And i dont just mean that its hard. I mean that it is hard in the most irritating ways possible. Slowing to a crawl every time you heal, being staggered by literally everything, stacking enemies right outside the boss door, refusing to fix the target-lock jank, summons that fail to show up to the arena, input constantly being eaten, estus flask randomly changing slots, etc. FromSoft have a funny way of polishing the mechanics on everything that kills you and letting everything that helps you be jank.

negative.original:
This is a terrible game. Maybe the worst game PC game I have ever played. They shove 10 different character classes in front of you at the start of the game and expect you to understand what each class does with no in-game information. I am not watching a youtube video or reading Reddit to learn how your game works. I am not doing homework for a video game. Forget that. 

I did video game homework to complete Tunic and I am not doing that again. All of the information on the game's systems should be in the game from the beginning. It doesn't have to be a mandatory tutorial but it needs to be available in the overworld before the first boss. 

All 10 classes have different stats and abilities and the game does not explain what these stats do or how to min max them Again, I am not doing homework for a video game. Put a textbox in the game and let me read how it works. I play games to relax, not whatever this is. 

The difficulty curve does not exist. They abolished the difficulty curve. Games are supposed to start off easy and get harder over time. I literally couldn't get past the first boss. Maybe if there was some sidequest or mini-game to do before the first boss I would stay in the game. But there is literally nothing to do in the starting area. There is nothing to explore. This is not an exploration focused game. 

And where is the difficulty slider? Are we just going to accept gaming companies like Fromsoft taking away difficulty sliders which have existed for decades? This is just enshittification of gaming. Who is going to put up with that? Why would you encourage a company to deliver a smaller product with fewer options?

negative.original:
tldr overrated as ♥♥♥♥, elden ring better if you are patient enough
ds1 is heaven, ds2 is purgatory and this game is hell. it keeps dragging me back to it even though i know damn well i won't have any fun playing it. it's so boring and there are so many better action games out there because this game basically cut all adventure notions from the 4 previous games (though few areas in the game have decent exploration and rewards for it) and it's not an improved rpg like dark souls 2 was, and the gameplay is worse than bloodborne.
what can i say ? the pvp is nice because of a solid community and decently designed areas for it, but the matchmaking system sucks ♥♥♥♥ compared to even dsr and you'll get smurfed everytime you start a new character
the second dlc is good but it requires you to play the first one which is underwhelming (while not terrible) and has a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ final boss to adress the "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ easy" complaints about base game.

not gonna make a long and exhaustive review as this game is almost 10 years old, but this game has many more issues which i'm not gonna cover since ds3 fans are insecure hypocrites and cannot stand criticism of their incredibly bland and flawed game. if you're not familiar with action rpgs, this may or may not be a good introduction as it is a very watered down and simplified game, however since it's still a soulsbornekiring game it still has hidden ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is hidden in a particularly stupid way in this game) which will reduce your gameplay options by a lot no matter what stats you invest into your first character. 

so really, i know bandai and the TERRIBLE modern fromsoft community's voice matters more than some weirdo who dares have his own idea of the game rather than getting it from the hivemind, but really, this game will hurt you more than can think. you will become a terrible person if you end up enjoying it, and you will become wrathful if you don't. you will pay not only with your money, but also with your soul

negative.original:
Dark Souls 3 has always been the souls game I liked the least, and I've always felt like the odd one for not glazing Dark Souls 3 as much as pretty much most Dark Souls fans.

Which is why I decided to give this game another try after having replayed Demon's Souls (PS3) recently, and after experiencing Bloodborne for the first time.

It's not really that hard to understand why most people would love Dark Souls 3 a lot, I personally can see why, unfortunately, Dark Souls 3 has crashed into the bottom of the barrel when it comes to Soulsborne games. While my re-playthrough was not as painful as the first, there are several things about Dark Souls 3 that just had me perplexed. How did FromSoftware came from a brilliant Bloodborne, to this?

Let's start with the good, the combat mechanics were revamped here to suit a faster paced combat like that of Bloodborne, and bringing back the magic system of Demon's Souls as well as adding unique weapon abilities. The soundtrack is still among From Software's best, and yes, there's a couple of great bosses in the game, specially on the DLCs.

Unfortunately, that's where most of my praise will end.

While the combat mechanics were revamped, they made a fatal mistake when it comes to balancing out enemies. Let's see Bloodborne for example, the game is extremely aggressive, and encourages aggressive playstyles for a Risk and Reward kind of gameplay. However, while Bloodborne is definitely brutal, it gives a fair challenge by letting you regain lost health for a small window with the Blood Rally system.

For Dark Souls 3? Not only are armors not upgradable, poise is almost non existent, you might as well just prioritize agility and dodge everything, because all enemies hit like a truck, and that becomes a balancing issue in the long term. The game actively encourages you to be aggressive, but at the same time it forces you to rely on your agility (AKA rolling) a bit too much. Enemies spam attacks way too much (even more than Bloodborne and Elden Ring), it almost feels like they have endless Stamina at times, which becomes highly annoying in the long term.

There's a difference between annoying good and annoying bad, a good annoying enemy will harass you if you let it, but it will teach you about itself as well as learning gameplay mechanics, in Dark Souls 3, enemies will simply not stop at all, and this becomes a little aggravating when you have to deal with several enemies at once when you less expect it. This means that you better master the art of roll at everything to either dodge or reposition yourself behind the enemy in order to backstab, ultimately transforming the game into a "Roll behind, and kill" kind of game, which becomes repetitive, might as well just call it "Rolling Souls" because that's the core of Dark Souls 3.

Setting aside the combat of Dark Souls 3, which is barely the least of the problems I have with the game, I'm gonna tackle the level design. After the brilliant interconnected world of Dark Souls 1 and Bloodborne, Dark Souls 3 takes 3 steps backwards, and becomes far more linear than Dark Souls 2, not like being linear is bad, mind you, but at times, it just feels like Dark Souls 3 has you on rails for most of the maps, which leads to some very baffling level designs that seemed like they actually wanted to make an interconnected world, but ultimately decided not to, but without removing the hints at it.

On several occasions, you'll find yourself at a place that has 1 or 2 locked doors that don't open from this side, that by the time you finally unlock them, it will be pointless, because you don't have to go there anymore. If the game wanted to be interconnected, then the unlocked path would be the equivalent of a shortcut path that leads to a bonfire, like heading down the elevator from that one Church in Dark Souls 1 to Firelink Shrine, or the breakable wall in Dark Souls 2's Forest of the Giants, for Dark Souls 3? this is kinda pointless, as you just reached another bonfire on the other side, which renders this pathway pointless to unlock.

Now, that's only the tip of the iceberg, there's far more ludicrous level design that's just baffling. From bonfires that are placed within literal meters from another one, to bonfires that are placed in the most inconvenient places possible that are probably meant to rage bait you. (Looking at that one Irithyl bonfire that's guarded by 2 annoying big ass dogs, which has an incredibly long ladder that could have been an elevator instead) Dark Souls 3 also started the trend of adding bonfires everywhere for no reason.

Last, but not least, there are two instances of the game where it's blocking a path with a "Does not open from this side" door, that might as well just be the most intelligence insulting level design, as you LITERALLY, just walk around a hole in the wall to find yourself on the other side of the very door that was locked, serving no real purpose as this could barely be considered a shortcut. Irythill Dungeon has this really goofy section and the Ashes of Ariandel DLC also does this by teasing a bonfire on the other side of a gate, only for you to just go through a hole in a wall and dropping into the bonfire that leads to the door that you can now open. Brilliant level design, Thanks Dark Souls 3.

And now, for the most aggravating part of the level design, is Dark Souls 3 committing sins through artificial difficulty. Now, don't get me wrong, most FromSoftware games will have at least 1 zone that feels cheap (Lost Izalith, Shrine of Amana, Lake of Rot, Valley of Defilement, Nightmare Frontier, you name it) but Dark Souls 3 quite easily outdoes every other game with either artificial difficulty, or extremely annoying to push through level design.

Farron Keep being a poison swamp with "slow water" effects is just a chore to go through, the path to Oceiros filled with some of the most annoying blob monsters ever, The Ringed City DLC Angels and Judicators spamming ranged attacks as if you were a cockroach fleeing from the kitchen, the hall with the oversized mutant flies in the Ariandel DLC, those enemies with arrows that explode on contact or the quake skill that can snipe you from afar even if you're technically no longer in that enemy's line of sight . The entire section of the Demon Ruins with a ballista terrorizing you, a Worm designed to one shot you, pyromancer monsters that spam fire orbs that spam fire attacks together. The jailers in Irythill Dungeon that reduces your max HP and makes you fat roll if touched. Archdragon peak with Titanite rocks that will push you off cliffs if you're not actively looking at every corner before, and much more.

At times, it just feels like DS3 was designed to piss you off, until you figure out that you have to go out of your way to deal with that thing that's preventing you from progressing at your own pace, it's like having the Bridge Wyvern from Dark Souls 1, put in several places, it just doesn't feel fun to traverse, even worse considering that most of these annoyances won't go away even after being killed (Judicators, for example).

For all the things that Dark Souls 3 may have exceeded at, Bloodborne did a lot better way before it. And not just that, Bloodborne generally felt more rewarding and fun to play, and for me, it has the least amount of issues in a FS title. Essentially, playing Bloodborne didn't made me like DS3 more than I hoped it would. Instead, it just made me understand my issues with it to a deeper level.

All in all, Dark Souls 3 can be a solid experience for the Combat Mechanics alone, which is what most people seems to like, as well as how that evens out with the fast paced boss fights, unfortunately, I was not able to ignore most of my grievances regarding DS3, because there is simply too many issues for me to ignore to be able enjoy the little good it offers.

translations.schinese:
Dark Souls 3 has always been the souls game I liked the least, and I've always felt like the odd one for not glazing Dark Souls 3 as much as pretty much most Dark Souls fans.

Which is why I decided to give this game another try after having replayed Demon's Souls (PS3) recently, and after experiencing Bloodborne for the first time.

It's not really that hard to understand why most people would love Dark Souls 3 a lot, I personally can see why, unfortunately, Dark Souls 3 has crashed into the bottom of the barrel when it comes to Soulsborne games. While my re-playthrough was not as painful as the first, there are several things about Dark Souls 3 that just had me perplexed. How did FromSoftware came from a brilliant Bloodborne, to this?

Let's start with the good, the combat mechanics were revamped here to suit a faster paced combat like that of Bloodborne, and bringing back the magic system of Demon's Souls as well as adding unique weapon abilities. The soundtrack is still among From Software's best, and yes, there's a couple of great bosses in the game, specially on the DLCs.

Unfortunately, that's where most of my praise will end.

While the combat mechanics were revamped, they made a fatal mistake when it comes to balancing out enemies. Let's see Bloodborne for example, the game is extremely aggressive, and encourages aggressive playstyles for a Risk and Reward kind of gameplay. However, while Bloodborne is definitely brutal, it gives a fair challenge by letting you regain lost health for a small window with the Blood Rally system.

For Dark Souls 3? Not only are armors not upgradable, poise is almost non existent, you might as well just prioritize agility and dodge everything, because all enemies hit like a truck, and that becomes a balancing issue in the long term. The game actively encourages you to be aggressive, but at the same time it forces you to rely on your agility (AKA rolling) a bit too much. Enemies spam attacks way too much (even more than Bloodborne and Elden Ring), it almost feels like they have endless Stamina at times, which becomes highly annoying in the long term.

There's a difference between annoying good and annoying bad, a good annoying enemy will harass you if you let it, but it will teach you about itself as well as learning gameplay mechanics, in Dark Souls 3, enemies will simply not stop at all, and this becomes a little aggravating when you have to deal with several enemies at once when you less expect it. This means that you better master the art of roll at everything to either dodge or reposition yourself behind the enemy in order to backstab, ultimately transforming the game into a "Roll behind, and kill" kind of game, which becomes repetitive, might as well just call it "Rolling Souls" because that's the core of Dark Souls 3.

Setting aside the combat of Dark Souls 3, which is barely the least of the problems I have with the game, I'm gonna tackle the level design. After the brilliant interconnected world of Dark Souls 1 and Bloodborne, Dark Souls 3 takes 3 steps backwards, and becomes far more linear than Dark Souls 2, not like being linear is bad, mind you, but at times, it just feels like Dark Souls 3 has you on rails for most of the maps, which leads to some very baffling level designs that seemed like they actually wanted to make an interconnected world, but ultimately decided not to, but without removing the hints at it.

On several occasions, you'll find yourself at a place that has 1 or 2 locked doors that don't open from this side, that by the time you finally unlock them, it will be pointless, because you don't have to go there anymore. If the game wanted to be interconnected, then the unlocked path would be the equivalent of a shortcut path that leads to a bonfire, like heading down the elevator from that one Church in Dark Souls 1 to Firelink Shrine, or the breakable wall in Dark Souls 2's Forest of the Giants, for Dark Souls 3? this is kinda pointless, as you just reached another bonfire on the other side, which renders this pathway pointless to unlock.

Now, that's only the tip of the iceberg, there's far more ludicrous level design that's just baffling. From bonfires that are placed within literal meters from another one, to bonfires that are placed in the most inconvenient places possible that are probably meant to rage bait you. (Looking at that one Irithyl bonfire that's guarded by 2 annoying big ass dogs, which has an incredibly long ladder that could have been an elevator instead) Dark Souls 3 also started the trend of adding bonfires everywhere for no reason.

Last, but not least, there are two instances of the game where it's blocking a path with a "Does not open from this side" door, that might as well just be the most intelligence insulting level design, as you LITERALLY, just walk around a hole in the wall to find yourself on the other side of the very door that was locked, serving no real purpose as this could barely be considered a shortcut. Irythill Dungeon has this really goofy section and the Ashes of Ariandel DLC also does this by teasing a bonfire on the other side of a gate, only for you to just go through a hole in a wall and dropping into the bonfire that leads to the door that you can now open. Brilliant level design, Thanks Dark Souls 3.

And now, for the most aggravating part of the level design, is Dark Souls 3 committing sins through artificial difficulty. Now, don't get me wrong, most FromSoftware games will have at least 1 zone that feels cheap (Lost Izalith, Shrine of Amana, Lake of Rot, Valley of Defilement, Nightmare Frontier, you name it) but Dark Souls 3 quite easily outdoes every other game with either artificial difficulty, or extremely annoying to push through level design.

Farron Keep being a poison swamp with "slow water" effects is just a chore to go through, the path to Oceiros filled with some of the most annoying blob monsters ever, The Ringed City DLC Angels and Judicators spamming ranged attacks as if you were a cockroach fleeing from the kitchen, the hall with the oversized mutant flies in the Ariandel DLC, those enemies with arrows that explode on contact or the quake skill that can snipe you from afar even if you're technically no longer in that enemy's line of sight . The entire section of the Demon Ruins with a ballista terrorizing you, a Worm designed to one shot you, pyromancer monsters that spam fire orbs that spam fire attacks together. The jailers in Irythill Dungeon that reduces your max HP and makes you fat roll if touched. Archdragon peak with Titanite rocks that will push you off cliffs if you're not actively looking at every corner before, and much more.

At times, it just feels like DS3 was designed to piss you off, until you figure out that you have to go out of your way to deal with that thing that's preventing you from progressing at your own pace, it's like having the Bridge Wyvern from Dark Souls 1, put in several places, it just doesn't feel fun to traverse, even worse considering that most of these annoyances won't go away even after being killed (Judicators, for example).

For all the things that Dark Souls 3 may have exceeded at, Bloodborne did a lot better way before it. And not just that, Bloodborne generally felt more rewarding and fun to play, and for me, it has the least amount of issues in a FS title. Essentially, playing Bloodborne didn't made me like DS3 more than I hoped it would. Instead, it just made me understand my issues with it to a deeper level.

All in all, Dark Souls 3 can be a solid experience for the Combat Mechanics alone, which is what most people seems to like, as well as how that evens out with the fast paced boss fights, unfortunately, I was not able to ignore most of my grievances regarding DS3, because there is simply too many issues for me to ignore to be able enjoy the little good it offers.

negative.original: My review is more an indictment on Steam and FromSoftware's optimization than it is on the content itself. I recommend this game fully FOR CONSOLE. Do not buy this on Steam, it is absolutely terrible. The game freezes and stutters constantly on a brand new high end 2025 PC (so does Elden Ring - it's a FromSoft thing).  Buyer beware because Steam wouldn't even refund mine. Had to download on a decade old PC which sadly runs the game better - though still frequent frame drops and freezes, pop-in and the like. Also ridiculous cost. $85 for a game that has been out for a decade. Seriously better off buying a console and staying away from this product on any Steam platform. You can get the game for $20 for PS4 to play on PS5 if you purchase from Amazon - I would recommend you do that.

negative.original:
sadly, I just cant get into it.
Combat feels extremely different from DS1 and 2, it feels more like bloodborne and elden ring (which I both enjoyed), but the big thing is the enemy attack patterns.
the enemys seem to just combo you into oblivion and never stop until your dead or you roll (which they also changed to be way shorter and have less i-frames).
Its a very linear game too, going in a straight line to the final boss, which takes away a lot of the exploration and freeroam-ness away.
The art style is definitely different too, looking less magical and more washed out and boring (in most places)
Bosses are alright, but most of them have some sort of gimmick that makes them really annoying, like constantly spawning in minions.
I really want to like this game, but its just not for me.
If you like bloodborne, elden ring, and soulless triple a games, this might be for you.

negative.original:
Dark Souls 3 is great game, kneecapped by the developers. MANY people love it, I personally think it is absolute garbage. Perhaps this is what people think of my love for the janky S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series or Jurassic Park: Tresspasser. I truly believe a lot of the love of Dark Souls is bad players taking pride in thier own "luck" with the boss run RNG after repeated attempts and thinking it is skill in this game, and being able to gloat at better players who gave up after too many bad experiences. Everything about this game makes me WANT to love it. Beautiful characters, gothic design, etc. But then I try playing it again after a year or two (I have much more time than it shows) and I am immediately reminded of the reasons I stopped playing the last time.

Honestly, the first boss is the perfect example of everything wrong with this game. Yes, I have beaten him many times. HOWEVER. Make a few attempts and you will notice the glaring issues. Damage can be completely random from the same attacks. This same boss can hit you twice (while being an estimated 5-10 feet from the end of his poleaxe if you dare to judge distance) and kill you while the next attempt you can get hit by the same attacks and be mostly fine. How about different runs where an enemy will make 5+ attacks in a row without pause, vs the next attempt where it attacks once and then just wanders around letting you hit it 5-6 times no problem (yeah, these are the runs you see recorded). Sometimes the game WILL just give you the middle finger on an attempt. How about having your character right up against the boss swinging and missing? (It seriously feels like Morrowind or Neverwinter Nights at times damage fails to register so often). And to crown it all, a boss who obscures the ENTIRE SCREEN constantly during the second phase so good luck lining up the attack or judging a dodge. Oh wait it isn't skill, it's luck luck LUCK!

Do you enjoy lining up your attacks (especially thrusts) only to have the attack go right through the enemy model and register NOTHING? How about hitting dodge only for it to do nothing (yes, even with FULL stamina)? Invincibility frames during the dodge (while in the air)... sometimes? There is input queing, but also a LOT of lost inputs. It is almost as if SOMETIMES your inputs get qued behind an enemy attack. 

Get used to it all. I mean... git gud?

I can get past most of the issues during "exploration" and I can live with the drug induced menu system, but once a boss hits I don't feel like having my time wasted after a few BS no chance runs. Give me Super Ghouls and Ghosts any day over this. If you want to be this difficult, your game needs to be TIGHT. The losses should feel like your fault alone. You should know a split second before you even take the hit what your mistake was. Being blindsided by the game wanting to steamroll you every once in a while just disrespects my time.

At the very least fix the input issues and fix the clipping/hitbox issues. Its been a bloody decade.

I truly believe a lot of the love of Dark Souls is bad players taking pride in thier own "luck" with the boss run RNG after repeated attempts and thinking it is skill in this game, and being able to gloat at better players who gave up after too many bad experiences. Everything about this game makes me WANT to love it. Beautiful characters, gothic design, etc. But then I try playing it again after a year or two (I have much more time than it shows) and I am immediately reminded of the reasons I stopped playing the last time.

Honestly, the first boss is the perfect example of everything wrong with this game. Yes, I have beaten him many times. HOWEVER. Make a few attempts and you will notice the glaring issues. Damage can be completely random from the same attacks. This same boss can hit you twice (while being an estimated 5-10 feet from the end of his poleaxe if you dare to judge distance) and kill you while the next attempt you can get hit by the same attacks and be mostly fine. How about different runs where an enemy will make 5+ attacks in a row without pause, vs the next attempt where it attacks once and then just wanders around letting you hit it 5-6 times no problem (yeah, these are the runs you see recorded). Sometimes the game WILL just give you the middle finger on an attempt. How about having your character right up against the boss swinging and missing? negative.original:
Simply awful.

I genuinely cannot find a single redeeming quality in this game. One of the worst gaming experiences I’ve ever had to date. This “thing” has to be one of the most overrated and overhyped pieces of software of all time. Think about everything you disliked in Elden Ring — now multiply the amount by 10 and the intensity by 10 — congratulations, you’ve got Dark Souls 3.
Released in 2016? This feels closer to TES: Oblivion than it does to Elden Ring. The game is rustic, outdated, sluggish, clunky, and downright revolting to play. The pacing feels like you’re stuck permanently at 0.75x speed. Animations are slow, inputs feel unresponsive, stamina management is sadistic, and the controls feel like they escaped from an alpha build. Menus are a chore, leveling up feels like paperwork, and basic actions feel worse than games released a decade earlier.
You like fighting bosses? So do I. Except here it’s not a boss-fighting game — it’s a run-back simulator. Every death means sprinting across the entire location again, dodging trash mobs, ambushes, and random nonsense just to attempt the boss one more time. “Oh but there are shortcuts” — yeah, not good enough, buddy. Elden Ring respects your time - this game actively despises it. There is not a single boss encounter that doesn’t feel padded with time-wasting misery beforehand. If Elden Ring is fun suffering, Dark Souls 3 is a fate worse than death.

Enemy design is cheap, hitboxes are questionable, tracking is absurd, and the game loves one-shotting you while laughing in your face. Gimmick bosses, jank physics, ambush spam — it’s all here, and none of it is fun. Skill often feels irrelevant when the game itself is fighting you harder than the enemies are.
Performance is a joke. I’m running this on an RTX 5080 and the game still freezes for up to 10 seconds at a time, repeatedly. How is this acceptable? There are far too many bugs, quirks, and “that’s just how it is” excuses for this to be considered a finished product, let alone a masterpiece.
If Elden Ring was your first Souls-like and you enjoyed it, do not buy this game. I was in that exact mindset, and my first 4 hours have been nothing but frustration, disbelief, and regret. The people who rate this game as a 10/10 or claim it’s their favorite either have nostalgia blindness, are lying to themselves, or should be locked up in an asylum.
60 euro? Asking anything more than 12 euro for this rusted pile of feces is a crime. This game does not deserve its reputation, its price, or its praise.
I recommend you never buy this, especially if Elden Ring was your entry into the genre.
APPALLING.

3/10

negative.original:
Don't buy games from this company. They can't even keep a game straight let alone price to what it's actually worth. When this game first released, I ranked this game a 8/10; Now I give it 4/10 due to it just being faildiver grade garbage. Publishers can't sell the game for what it's worth so It's still a dead game (Only ppl playing are playing pointless PvP) and developers can't stop micro managing tweeker exploits. After the company lost it's major contributor to the games development, it clearly started diving, more than expected, incomparison to what it was before. Take for example when Elden Ring released and they took the servers down for a few days while they brought Elden Ring into the mix. Upon the servers coming back online, they brought in a security violation, that allowed invading players to gain access to you PC. Took them 3 months to take the servers down and even recognize it as a problem (Not a good sign for things to come). Fast forward till a few months ago and I seen they reopened up the servers and so I thought I would put Valhiem down and try this game out again for nastalgia sake. It's been a hot minute since I played it so I figured it would take me abit to get back into it but I mean it's liek riding a bike right. 1500hrs in just DS3, i think i can relearn how to play the game pretty easily or with out too much frustration. Yeah that's a lie and it's not cause this game is "Hard". I play Vanilla Valhiem and solo the game; learning curves can be fun, except when the designers of that playground are a bunch Tweeking Reactors. What's that, you might ask. Just when a developer is so bored with thier job and can't honestly do anything to make their product better, based on thier own experience and developer skillset and understanding of gaming in general and can only watch a bunch Greedy Twitchers, show people how to exploit their garbage and then go to work and react to it with some nerfs and buffs and micro-changes. (I'll get into that in a hot minute).

Let's take lock on mechanics for example. That was one thing that I thought was gonna get better when Elden Ring came out. Boy was I wrong. If i thought locking onto an enemy on the opposite side of the arena, that I'm not even looking at, was kind of dumb, well Elden Ring has a present for you. These devs could only figure out how to make worse and then just ignore it. Why? Guess it's a hard mechanic to adjust, so ur character is gonna lock onto the target that is engaged in combat with you, let alone how bout those guys sitting on the ground in front of me? No. Gonna lock onto the dude that's through 2 walls, a floor and a pillar; Yup makes sense. No definetly don't want to lock onto the enemy that's pounding my health into lunchables. No that would mean you developers actually know what your doing and not just flip some assests and make them look pretty with an edgy mystery for a story behind it? Oh wait that is literally what your entire franchise has become, which is why it needs to be run by a modding community. When you guys as developers can't make a game with out everyone patching it to be 'Fun', then yes you guys have an issue to address, but lack the skill set or life experience to do that.

I'm not paying for this Faildiver grade learning curve. I bought Elden Ring hoping that things about this franchise would improve, but rather than building off of logic, you developers just chased exploits and meta like the tweekers you go home to watch after 'work'. Never bought Elden Ring DLC and I won't and I will never buy Nightreign, becuz they follow the same dumb logic (Which is a complete lack there of).

So why my complaint here? Cuz I used to play this game alot, but after putting it down and coming back I relealized you devs have made enough minor changes to the way enemies/bosses work that now the game no longer feels like a form of combat rhythm, where boss battles and the region before the boss were all like a song of combat. Not anymore. Now it's a running simulator to the next BFG-Meta, to explode a boss and repeat till the end game. Same as Elden Ring. Boring Hot Garbage. This game has lost it combat finesse. Dark souls 1 used to be alot more styled like a live action DnD, but people wanted more anime flare, so i guess the devs decided to put some of that illogical game mechanic into the series. I'm not against it as long as it balances in properly and doesn't make old mechanics obsolete or useless. It didn't. In fact becuase the devs don't know how to develope properly, they would blanket patch things till those exploits became more 'Game' like and less 'exlpoity' in thier opinion. These blanket patches would also screw-over other classes or open up the avenue for new exploits, of which this is now what this game and other games from this franchise, have become. Developer go home and watch tweeker play game, go to work now with new reason for work and react to exploit with an exploit against that exploit. Yea F this. Don't believe me, watch twtichers play this game. In 15 mins you'll see it's like I said, chase an exploit to blow up a boss, while turning the rest of the game into forgettable running simulator.

Here's some examples. I went around the game to see where the kick mechanic was acutally applicable, cause I mean not only is it a pourly mapped mechanic, that seems to get you killed more then it comes in handy, but I mean seriously it's gotta have a use right? On enemies hiding behind sheilds, but even then, it doesn't do that much stamina damage to be worth it. Take for example the grave wardens. Ever tried kicking those guys, cuz for a light armored enemy that moves around like they got rockets on Ice Skates this is beyond stupid. Not only do they spam attack like they have no stamina bar (But my character does.. Give the enemy a stamina bar to manage like me not a spam button), but they also have moves that have inifinite posise or extreme poise for thier speed and maneuverability. When you kick them, you can see; It does nothing. It's like this with alot of enemies. So you ask yourself, why did they include it in future games or why not make it toggleable for those that like to use it? Probably for the same reasons these devs can't firgure out how to not make a one hit wonder and success for someone else to make big hits off of. For the same reasons these devs can't figure out how to play the game and not chase and react to metas they watched tweekers do. Take for example the infinity stamina bar. Fighting Champion Gundyr, I relalised ppl parrying the boss all the time has caused you devs to nerf his period inbetween combos so that he is spaming his combos liek the gravewardens. Now there's basically only one or 2 ways to kill gundyr cause he got patch-reacted, to the point that if you are trying any other way to kill him; unistall the game and play something else. This franchise can only chase meta that a modding community figured out how to balance or fix properly. Don't give money to a franchise that needs to be bought out, cause all they can do is come out with flashy edgelord garbage and react to some tweekers. In enjoyed the combat challeneges this game used to have. Now the only Dark Soul is the Void that is these devs capabilities (Didn't know the flame burning out was a metaphor for you devs being burn outs. Didn't know the Rot was you devs all along)

negative.original:
There's a good reason even the delusional fromsoft fanboys tend to ♥♥♥♥ on this one. The online connectivity is leagues worse than previous entries, the input delay is the worst of any game I have ever played in my entire life, and enemy design aspires to be as infuriatingly unbalanced and unfun as possible; massively bloated healthbars and damage numbers, weirdly poor player health scaling (the actual numbers behind the vigor stat are baffling considering how hard enemies hit you), poise is entirely replaced by 'hyperarmor' that only affects certain weapon types (zero information in-game btw), teleporting enemies, absurdly bad hitboxes that make ds2 haters look clinically insane, and grab attacks that casually instakill or send you out of bounds.

And in-case you're wondering, the camera is still sm64 levels of awful.

negative.original:
Hoo boy I might get flack for this. Take it with a grain of salt.

This is a good game, but after 100%ing it I cannot recommend it. Unless you've played at least DSI/ the remastered version, there is literally no reason to play DSIII. It is fanservice incarnate for the series, a love letter, which is great. The community is hit or miss. Co-oping bosses can be fun, and it is satisfying, but pvp is not. Whoever lags the most essentially wins. Online is a joke - servers buffer in and out, and Bandai Namco (the publisher) does not fix this often. It is possible to play offline completely, and I recommend that if you plan on playing DSIII.

That being said, there is a lot to love. Magic is the weakest in this game, you can't stack spells or recover, and this going forward is the template which inspired Elden Ring and Night Reign as I understand it - if you've played either this isn't difficult. That's typically how I see whether a game in this genre is good - if it handles magic correctly, whether that's lightning, dark, or regular sorceries. If you like DSI but not II, you will this one, and that goes for the wider community at large. I see why. But it has missed potential.

A lot of things wrap up. My experience was starting here first cause I heard about it being the easiest to start - you have to remember that people who play these games aren't always the best judge at where to start. For them, it might have been easier because at that point they had played a lot, but honestly any game is good to start playing all of them now imo.

Story is non-existent. That's a thing in this series, but there is a lot of lore. You have to explore, interact with NPCs. Likely, you'll play multiple NGs or above if you stick with it. This game is much more polished than the previous two, but at the sacrifice of its soul. The last boss feels superfluous, and I'm not sure if that was the point, but unlike the final boss of the first or second installment, there is not as much weight. The plot sort of... meanders. I'm just going to go with that

As an aside, do not complete this game 100% if you plan on playing it. Getting all achievements took most my playtime (a typical first playthrough is 30 hrs, a fast one is 8-10 if you do everything plus DLC). Let that sit: I played 3+ characters, one of them to NG++. This is a thing in the second as well, somewhat the first, but it can exponentially increase the playtime if you do everything legit. If you don't do online it's even harder, just search covenants and spell rewards and you'll see what I mean.

Suffice to say, how I see it games are meant to be enjoyed or at the very least act as art- I liked Dark Souls III, but I have the inclination to its vibe and aesthetic, and for most people I do not recommend it. To summarize, it is good, but it is more for fans if anything, and 100%ing it I am now definitely burned out with any Fromsoft game for awhile yet. Had fun though, I can say that.

For them, it might have been easier because at that point they had played a lot, but honestly any game is good to start playing all of them now imo.

Story is non-existent. That's a thing in this series, but there is a lot of lore. You have to explore, interact with NPCs. Likely, you'll play multiple NGs or above if you stick with it. This game is much more polished than the previous two, but at the sacrifice of its soul. The last boss feels superfluous, and I'm not sure if that was the point, but unlike the final boss of the first or second installment, there is not as much weight. The plot sort of... meanders. I'm just going to go with that

As an aside, do not complete this game 100% if you plan on playing it. Getting all achievements took most my playtime (a typical first playthrough is 30 hrs, a fast one is 8-10 if you do everything plus DLC). Let that sit: I played 3+ characters, one of them to NG++. This is a thing in the second as well, somewhat the first, but it can exponentially increase the playtime if you do everything legit. If you don't do online it's even harder, just search covenants and spell rewards and you'll see what I mean.

Suffice to say, how I see it games are meant to be enjoyed or at the very least act as art- I liked Dark Souls III, but I have the inclination to its vibe and aesthetic, and for most people I do not recommend it. To summarize, it is good, but it is more for fans if anything, and 100%ing it I am now definitely burned out with any Fromsoft game for awhile yet. Had fun though, I can say that.

negative.original:
It's a very good game, however the amount of quality and enjoyment is offset heavily by how annoying it can be. 

I could rave on about how the introductory phase of the game (high wall of lothric) is terrible and does a terrible job at being an early game place, I could complain about how annoying PvP is with majority of my experience being dying because my opponent has a giant strength weapon that cleaves 1/3 of my health with a regular attack and always staggers me long enough that I can't roll, leading me to getting hit again for another 1/3 of my health. 

I could talk about how the game hates telling you anything considering how sparse information is, I could talk about how disconnected the story and world felt from gameplay because all the lore is only really in the many, many item descriptions. 

I could even talk about the smaller annoyances like the poison gimmick of Farron Keep being stupid because It deals so little damage I can outheal it with gentle prayer and the most annoying part of the area is actually how slow you have to trudge through the mud or the system of dropping all your souls on death and then losing them forever if you don't pick them up or die again. 

But I won't go into those points because ultimately it doesn't matter, at the end of the day all of those aspects are annoying and not fun so when the entire experience is filled with annoying experiences it doesn't matter if I put it in the ridiculous time sink to 100% the game because I wanted to. When I remember this game months or years after putting it down the first thing that will come to my mind is not the great bossfight experiences I had but that "oh yeah that game was really annoying to play, why did I even 100% it?"

Still, I want to thank my friend who gave me the key for the game cause who is paying $60 USD for a 10 year old game they don't even bother to fix the bugs in. No seriously the archers in Lothric Castle shoot through the walls and I've gotten a bug where my entire screen is covered in items with Chinese text twice.

negative.original: The following points I am sharing about the game are material observations about the game and not based upon any emotional sway of the game: The dark souls games are absolutely not fair, and are not designed to be intentionally. It punishes behaviour often randomly and regardless of skill level. It relies on past knowledge and memorizing hitboxes and various illegible things in order to get better. I have completed ds1 and 2 and am halfway through 3. This is a consistent design philosophy throughout. growing as a player is sidelined for grinding for levels and items, unearned knowledge about the game through brute force dying and going back with prior knowledge. There are literally impossible to avoid things without dying to them first. You will assume there is a deeper mechanic to dark souls than that, but no, it is actually that shallow often. It is lovely to explore new environments and the vibes are great, and minibosses can be fun. Lots of builds to explore and routes to go through. Fundamentally disrespectful and *unfair* game loop, objectively.

negative.original:
This game struggles with a severe lack of information. Items, abilities, enemies, mechanics, and even maps are poorly explained, if at all. From the UI alone, it’s often impossible to tell what an item or ability actually does. While experimentation is clearly intended, the sheer number of items makes this approach more frustrating than rewarding. The game can be borderline unplayable without searching for answers from online.

Player invasions are another low point. Being attacked by another player while already dealing with difficult enemies is infuriating. Playing offline avoids this, but at the cost of losing player messages, which are often genuinely helpful or amusing.

Where the game truly excels is in the heat of combat. Finishing a tough boss or landing a perfectly timed dodge against a massive enemy attack feels incredible. Combined with its dark, grotesque art direction and oppressive atmosphere, these moments show the game at its best, even if its systems often work against the player.

negative.original:
Platinumed on ps. My favorite of the series
EDIT: unplayable on PC with xbox bluetooth controller. Game freezes randomly and often, sometimes for minutes at a time. When I disconnect Controller and play w/ keyboard, unfortuntely it runs perfectly so I know the controller is causing the issue. Not being able to play with controller is unacceptable for me, no fix seems available, this seems to be a known issue, and Steam explicitly does not offer support for this title. Do not buy this game if you use xbox bluetooth controller!

When I disconnect Controller and play w/ keyboard, unfortuntely it runs perfectly so I know the controller is causing the issue. Not being able to play with controller is unacceptable for me, no fix seems available, this seems to be a known issue, and Steam explicitly does not offer support for this title. Do not buy this game if you use xbox bluetooth controller!

negative.original:
Inferior in all aspects to first dark souls 
Badly designed weapons system and the game relies on having more enemies instead of better enemies 
65% of locations are just swarms of tall hollows with rediculous amount of hp
If youre playing slow swinging weapon youre playing on extra hard mode as half the bosses will be able to stun you even if you attacked first

Half areas feel somewhat like dark souls especially start and final areas but around half of them are just so boring, repetetive and soulless it is just a pain. Even lost Izalyth which i found the worst part of dark souls one had more soul to it the half the locations in this game.
It is still at least a 6.4/10 game and it has its moments but it does not live up the the masterpiece that was the first Dark souls.

This is the Best FromSoftware Game.

That being said, i cannot recommend this version of the game considering the game consistently stutters and they are charging $80 for it.

This game is available on Xbox and Ps4 -5 and runs at 60fps with no stutters. The game is worth it. spend your money there if you NEED to play it. There are no real fixes for these stutters.

negative.original:
This is the worst purchase I've made in years. For how much it costs, even on sale, I'd expect the game to be well balanced and designed but there are major flaws with it. Go with Dark Souls 1 or 2 instead, I do not recommend this game even on sale.

I went with the build concept of a sword-and-board heavily armored knight. This is literally the posterchild build for the franchise, even. Every game's cover art is a knight in plate armor with a straight sword, and "John Souls" characters are made with this build. But for DS3 it's not a practical option.

For some reason there's a one-two combo of gameplay changes they made in 3 that made the posterchild build of the game impractical this time.

First off: armor got straight nerfed hard. Being armored in 3 isn't much more protecting than being naked. And in fact, the best protection by far is dodge rolling so you're better off ditching armor so you can do better dodge rolls. This used to just be a subjective recommendation by min-maxers, but now it's a pretty objective recommendation. You can wear clothes of course, just make sure your dodge rolls are fast as hell and get you far from dager.

Then second: almost half the enemies in 3 do as much damage, if not more, as the bosses did in the other games. So now the posterchild armor is hindering more than protecting to begin with, but also every other enemy you meet can demolish your shield and destroy you like a Dark Souls boss.

But wait, there's more! Dark Souls 3 added a "mechanic" where doing co-op was seen as a signal that you wanted more online interaction. What this meant is that if you ever summon or are summoned to co-op, the servers will put you on the priority list for PvP invasions.

I'm guessing this is why despite having almost double the active player count, 3's co-op is dead as hell while 2's co-op is actually active. If 3's co-op players are constantly being killed and locked out of co-op just because they did co-op, it's no wonder there won't be many players able to co-op.

Someone made some crazy bad design decisions for the game's underlying mechanics, and it seems the franchise hype insulated the game from the criticism it deserved. I've seen other games with smaller problems get far worse reviews.

Go buy Dark Souls Remastered or Dark Souls 2. Or maybe Elden Ring, I don't know since I bought DS3 instead. I wanted to stick to franchise loyalty or w/e this concept is called, but consider my franchise loyalty crushed.

translations.german:
This is the worst purchase I've made in years. For how much it costs, even on sale, I'd expect the game to be well balanced and designed but there are major flaws with it. Go with Dark Souls 1 or 2 instead, I do not recommend this game even on sale.

I went with the build concept of a sword-and-board heavily armored knight. This is literally the posterchild build for the franchise, even. Every game's cover art is a knight in plate armor with a straight sword, and "John Souls" characters are made with this build. But for DS3 it's not a practical option.

For some reason there's a one-two combo of gameplay changes they made in 3 that made the posterchild build of the game impractical this time.

First off: armor got straight nerfed hard. Being armored in 3 isn't much more protecting than being naked. And in fact, the best protection by far is dodge rolling so you're better off ditching armor so you can do better dodge rolls. This used to just be a subjective recommendation by min-maxers, but now it's a pretty objective recommendation. You can wear clothes of course, just make sure your dodge rolls are fast as hell and get you far from dager.

Then second: almost half the enemies in 3 do as much damage, if not more, as the bosses did in the other games. So now the posterchild armor is hindering more than protecting to begin with, but also every other enemy you meet can demolish your shield and destroy you like a Dark Souls boss.

negative.original:
I like Souls-likes, but Dark Souls 3 felt more punishing to my time than to my skill. While learning, I often died to long runbacks or to the controls, healing when I meant to attack, or vice versa, even on controller.

Who thought it was a good idea to put enemies between a bonfire and a boss? I can see why this works for veterans, but as a newer player it felt antiquated and frustrating. I wouldn’t recommend it unless you’re already used to older Souls design.

negative.original: Not for me. Played it a few months ago around Christmas cause I wanted a game where I could be a Knight, and the combat is fairly fun as well as the graphics being beautiful. The game runs nicely on a lower end budget PC like mine, but I have my issues with the game. At first it was button queueing, where I'd press dodge twice in a hurry to dodge once and after the first roll was done, it'd roll again. This caused me some issues and it took some getting used to, but after 3 or 4 months I came back just using the block with the shield and was able to beat the first boss fairly easily, didn't use any heals. My biggest issue is enemy arrows phasing through enemies to home in on you instead of coming into contact with them and damaging them, something I've never seen in any game before now. And it kinda pissed me off, cause I was doing well, I'd only used one health thing and the combat and such was fun, but this caused me my first death as I expected it to hit the enemy but instead if phased through the already low health enemy, hit me, cancelled my attack and got me killed since I was low on health after being surrounded. I was not very happy. Of course the game is good, I won't say it isn't good, it's one of the best games of all time from what I've seen, it's just not for me, the control system and arrows in general. I'm sure someone else will find it much more fun, I just can't enjoy it.

This caused me some issues and it took some getting used to, but after 3 or 4 months I came back just using the block with the shield and was able to beat the first boss fairly easily, didn't use any heals. My biggest issue is enemy arrows phasing through enemies to home in on you instead of coming into contact with them and damaging them, something I've never seen in any game before now. And it kinda pissed me off, cause I was doing well, I'd only used one health thing and the combat and such was fun, but this caused me my first death as I expected it to hit the enemy but instead if phased through the already low health enemy, hit me, cancelled my attack and got me killed since I was low on health after being surrounded. I was not very happy. Of course the game is good, I won't say it isn't good, it's one of the best games of all time from what I've seen, it's just not for me, the control system and arrows in general. I'm sure someone else will find it much more fun, I just can't enjoy it.
